defects: Decimal addition had no rounding policy; cents-rounded implementations passed all old fixtures.

objective: Find the first exact string match while preserving the original record identity and data.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Find and exact string equality remain supported.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Selecting an existing application record is a direct engineering operation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: First-match, no-match and reference identity generalize to lookups.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded string names and plain records fit the introductory find task.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Correct record selection avoids modest case/identity mistakes.

defects: Structural comparison accepted a clone rather than the original user object.
Name equality rules were unstated; case-insensitive lookup passed the old fixtures.
Input preservation and bounded string-comparison cost needed explicit assumptions.
rationale: The revised brief specifies first original-object identity, exact case/space/empty-string matching, undefined for absence, unchanged plain records and names of at most 128 UTF-16 units. Direct identity assertions distinguish a clone from a found record; duplicate, case, empty, spaced and canonically different Unicode names are covered. The existing hint is sound but narrow: it helps distinguish one element from an array without teaching a full matching strategy.

objective: Construct an inclusive ascending integer interval and reason about output-sized work.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Loops, generators and array construction remain supported.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Integer intervals support pagination and test-data generation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Inclusive bounds and output-size reasoning transfer to enumeration.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Small integer endpoints and reversed intervals fit a foundation task.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Explicit endpoints prevent modest off-by-one and allocation mistakes.

defects: Reversed endpoints and input bounds were unspecified.
An implementation memorizing the old finite fixture table passed.
The old hint directly stated the loop recipe instead of boundary reasoning.
rationale: The interval now handles equal and reversed endpoints explicitly, with integer endpoints between -10,000 and 10,000. Its n is the output length rather than either endpoint magnitude. Array.from, for-loop, generator and independent while-loop alternatives pass, including the 20,001-element boundary and a whole 128-element interval. End-exclusive, empty-singleton and fixture-only implementations fail.
